faqs.question: What is the difference between a CMS and a website builder?
faqs.answer: The categories overlap. Compare structured content, editorial workflows, visual design, hosting, maintenance, and portability against the site you need to run.

faqs.question: Are the prices and ratings verified?
faqs.answer: No. Current prices, ratings, and plan limits have not been independently verified. Confirm current details with vendor documentation.

faqs.question: What SEO controls should I test?
faqs.answer: Check titles, descriptions, canonical URLs, redirects, sitemap output, indexation settings, structured data support, and the rendered output.

faqs.question: How should I evaluate editorial workflows?
faqs.answer: Ask an editor to draft, revise, submit for review, publish, and roll back a page. Check permissions, revision history, scheduling, and reusable content.

faqs.question: Can I migrate away later?
faqs.answer: Test export of content, media, URLs, metadata, and redirects. Estimate the work required to recreate layouts, forms, and integrations elsewhere.

faqs.question: What costs should I include?
faqs.answer: Include the platform plan, hosting, seats, templates, plugins, integrations, support, maintenance, backups, security updates, and staff time.

author: Emily Nakamura
body:
CMS and Website Publishing Platforms: Buyer’s Guide

CMS products and website builders overlap, but differ in design workflow, structured content, editorial controls, hosting, extensibility, and maintenance. Choose according to the site you need to operate, not a generic ranking.

Transparency note: Current prices, ratings, plan limits, and product claims have not been independently verified for this shortlist. Confirm details in current vendor documentation before buying.

Platforms to evaluate

Webflow

Test visual design, CMS collections, editor permissions, redirects, accessibility, publishing, localization, and export options. Confirm hosting and feature limits for your site.

Framer

Test responsive layouts, content updates by non-designers, metadata, redirects, analytics, accessibility, and whether the content model fits the site.

Wix

Test the editor with the staff who will maintain the site. Verify forms, SEO controls, redirects, integrations, backups, and the plan required for business features.

WordPress

Evaluate editorial flexibility and extensibility alongside responsibility for hosting, updates, backups, plugin compatibility, security, and recovery.

Evaluation checklist

  1. Define page types, content relationships, languages, forms, and editorial roles.
  2. Test the full publishing process: draft, review, publish, revise, and roll back.
  3. Check title and description controls, canonical URLs, redirects, sitemap output, structured data support, and indexing settings.
  4. Test keyboard navigation, headings, contrast, and form labels on representative templates.
  5. Document responsibility for hosting, backups, updates, security, analytics, and incidents.
  6. Test export of content, media, URLs, metadata, and redirects.
  7. Calculate the cost of hosting, seats, plugins, integrations, support, and maintenance.

Pricing and limitations

Costs vary by site plan, hosting, seats, content limits, plugins, integrations, and maintenance. Current pricing and plan limits are not independently verified. Check official pricing and include ongoing operating effort in the comparison.

Methodology

This is a practical evaluation framework, not a verified rating leaderboard, ROI estimate, or universal recommendation. Test publishing, SEO controls, accessibility, portability, and cost for your actual project.
